prompt: To MOVE a π bond (alkene) from one position to another (e.g., 1-pentene → 2-pentene), the general strategy is:

options.label: Add HX or H₂O to the π bond, then eliminate (E2) in a different direction to form the new alkene
π bonds can't be moved — the position of a C=C is fixed once formed
Heat alone — thermal isomerization moves alkenes to the thermodynamically most stable position
LiAlH₄ migrates π bonds by hydride shuttle across the molecule

explanation: Convert the π bond to an sp³ intermediate (alkyl halide or alcohol), then eliminate to form the new π bond on an adjacent position. Choice of Zaitsev vs Hofmann elimination tunes direction. Simple heat doesn't isomerize alkenes under neutral conditions (needs acid/base catalyst).
